title: Kinematics
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for IB Diploma Physics (status of the source: ai-reviewed-reverified-gate-verified-2026-09-29-awaiting-human-signoff). Terms and clues: A.1.7#xt1 term and clue written for the game; A.1.9#xt2 term and clue written for the game; A.1.8#xt1 term and clue written for the game; A.1.9#xt1 term and clue written for the game. assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Acceleration
items.clue: The rate of change of velocity; the gradient of a velocity–time graph.

items.label: Terminal speed
items.clue: The constant value reached by a falling body once the drag on it balances its weight.

items.label: Projectile
items.clue: A body that, after launch, moves freely under the action of gravity alone in the ideal case.

items.label: Fluid resistance
items.clue: The drag from air or a liquid that makes a real trajectory asymmetric, with a steeper descent.

questions.stem: A car starts from rest and moves along a straight road. Its acceleration is greatest at the start and decreases continuously, falling quickly at first and then more slowly, but stays positive, until the car reaches 20 m s⁻¹ at t = 10 s. Which gives the distance travelled by the car in these 10 s?

options.text: Between 100 m and 200 m, since its speed rises fastest early on
Exactly 100 m, as its average velocity is (0 + 20)/2 m s⁻¹
Exactly 200 m, as it moves at 20 m s⁻¹ for the whole 10 s
Less than 100 m, as the curve of its velocity–time graph bends upwards

questions.explanation: The velocity–time graph rises steeply and then flattens, so it lies above the straight line from (0, 0) to (10 s, 20 m s⁻¹), whose area is 100 m. The velocity stays below 20 m s⁻¹ until t = 10 s, so the area is also less than 20 × 10 = 200 m.

questions.stem: A ball is kicked horizontally at 12 m s⁻¹ from the top of a vertical cliff 20 m high and lands on level ground below. Fluid resistance is negligible. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². How far from the foot of the cliff does the ball land?
questions.explanation: Vertically, the ball starts with zero vertical velocity: 20 = ½ × 9.8 × t², so t = 2.02 s. Horizontally, its velocity stays 12 m s⁻¹, so it travels 12 × 2.02 = 24 m.

questions.stem: A small steel ball is released from rest in air and falls until it reaches terminal speed. How does its acceleration change during this time?

options.text: It is constant but less than g, because fluid resistance is constant.
It stays equal to g, since fluid resistance only lowers the ball's speed.
It increases, since the ball moves faster and faster as it falls.
It decreases from g towards zero as the fluid resistance increases.

questions.explanation: At release the ball is at rest, so there is no fluid resistance and its acceleration is g. As it speeds up the fluid resistance grows, so its acceleration decreases, reaching zero at terminal speed.

questions.stem: A graph of velocity against time for a sprinter starts at the origin, rises steeply, becomes gradually less steep, and is a horizontal line at 11 m s⁻¹ from t = 6.0 s until the end of the race. Which describes the sprinter's motion?

options.text: The acceleration decreases, so the sprinter is slowing down after the start.
The acceleration increases, since the sprinter keeps getting faster.
The acceleration falls to zero, and the sprinter is at rest after 6.0 s.
The acceleration falls to zero while the speed rises to a steady value.

questions.explanation: The gradient of a velocity–time graph is the acceleration. The gradient decreases from a large value to zero at t = 6.0 s, while the height, the velocity, rises to 11 m s⁻¹ and then stays constant.

questions.stem: A ball is kicked from level ground at 20.0 m s⁻¹ at 30.0° above the horizontal. Fluid resistance is negligible. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the maximum height reached by the ball?
questions.explanation: The vertical component of the launch velocity is 20.0 sin 30.0° = 10.0 m s⁻¹. At the maximum height the vertical velocity is zero, so 0 = 10.0² − 2 × 9.8 × h, giving h = 5.10 m.

questions.stem: A small plastic ball is launched without spin from level ground at 30° above the horizontal. The motion is compared with an identical launch in which fluid resistance is negligible. Which describes the effect of fluid resistance on the ball's motion?

options.text: The range is shorter, and the horizontal velocity component decreases during the flight.
The range is shorter, but the horizontal velocity component stays constant in flight.
The range is shorter, and the highest point is still reached at exactly half the range.
The range is unchanged, as the ball follows the same path but moves more slowly.

questions.stem: A stone is thrown from the top of a cliff at 15.0 m s⁻¹ at 30.0° below the horizontal. It lands in the sea 40.0 m below the point of release. Fluid resistance is negligible. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². How long after release does the stone reach the sea?
questions.explanation: The initial vertical velocity is 15.0 sin 30.0° = 7.50 m s⁻¹ downwards. With downwards positive, 40.0 = 7.50t + 4.9t², whose positive root is t = 2.19 s.

questions.stem: Ball X, of mass 0.20 kg, rolls off a horizontal table top at 3.0 m s⁻¹. At the same instant ball Y, of mass 0.40 kg, is released from rest at the same height. Fluid resistance is negligible. Which ball reaches the floor first?

options.text: Y lands first, as X's horizontal motion keeps it in the air longer.
Y lands first, as a heavier ball falls with greater acceleration.
X lands first, as its greater speed carries it down faster.
They land together, as both start with zero vertical velocity.

questions.explanation: The horizontal and vertical motions are independent. Both balls start with zero vertical velocity, fall the same height and have the same vertical acceleration, g, so they take the same time. X's horizontal velocity only decides where it lands.

questions.stem: A ball is launched at 40° above the horizontal over level ground. Fluid resistance is negligible. Which statement describes the ball at its highest point?

options.text: Its velocity is momentarily zero; its acceleration is g downwards.
Its velocity is horizontal and non-zero; its acceleration is g downwards.
Its velocity is horizontal and non-zero; it has no acceleration.
Its horizontal velocity is less than at launch; its acceleration is g downwards.

questions.explanation: At the highest point the vertical component of velocity is zero, but the horizontal component, u cos 40°, is unchanged, so the velocity is horizontal. The only acceleration throughout the flight is g downwards.
